mechanism: structured_checkpoint compaction carries all cross-compaction state as prose: the previous checkpoint is re-presented to the summarizer as ordinary compressible transcript on every subsequent compaction, and the agent's own tool-derived file operations exist nowhere except that prose. Repeated compaction therefore erodes both stated facts and the agent's record of what it did.
hypothesis: The operative knob is the compaction strategy, not its parameters or prompt. G4 states three heterogeneous facts early, then compacts 4-6 times; the file paths are gone in 3/3 attempts while the most recently stated fact survives, the signature of a checkpoint being re-compressed each round rather than carried forward as settled state. G5 writes two files via tools and is asked what it did; in both completed attempts the model recalls only the later write, because file operations are reconstructed from summarizer prose rather than extracted from tool calls. No compaction_prompt edit can fix this: the summarizer is structurally shown the same content as both settled state and compressible input, and instructions cannot make a model stop compressing what it is asked to compress. Carbon ships a vetted alternative on the menu, token_budget_checkpoint, whose incremental checkpoints remove the prior checkpoint from the compressible middle and whose deterministic state re-attaches tool-derived file paths verbatim.
